title.ja: D1 に親しんだ人の SQL 開発: Aurora DSQL、RDS PostgreSQL、Aurora Serverless v2
title.en: SQL Development for D1 Users: Aurora DSQL, RDS PostgreSQL, and Aurora Serverless v2

sources.title: What is Amazon Aurora DSQL?
supports: Aurora DSQL is available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo), ap-northeast-1
Serverless, with no instances to provision; data is replicated synchronously across three Availability Zones
Currently compatible with PostgreSQL version 16
ACID transactions with strong consistency and snapshot isolation
Multi-Region clusters must stay inside one Region set; Tokyo, Osaka, and Seoul are in the Asia Pacific set

sources.title: Migrating from PostgreSQL to Aurora DSQL
supports: The isolation level is fixed at PostgreSQL Repeatable Read
DDL and DML need separate transactions; a transaction holds one DDL statement; a transaction modifies at most 3,000 rows
Connections time out after 1 hour
One built-in database named postgres per cluster; UTF-8, C collation only, UTC
No temporary tables, no triggers, no PL/pgSQL (SQL functions only); DELETE FROM or DROP/CREATE instead of TRUNCATE; CREATE INDEX ASYNC instead of CREATE INDEX
Foreign keys are supported
Conflicts return a serialization error instead of waiting for a lock; AWS recommends idempotent transactions with retry, and random primary keys
Permissions are schema-level grants: admin manages objects in public, non-admin roles use user-created schemas

sources.title: Supported SQL for Aurora DSQL
supports: BEGIN accepts ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ and READ WRITE | READ ONLY
INSERT supports ON CONFLICT; SELECT supports FOR UPDATE and FOR KEY SHARE, joins, CTEs, and window functions
CREATE SCHEMA, CREATE VIEW, CREATE SEQUENCE, CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE SQL, and CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC are supported
The page says the list is not exhaustive

sources.title: DDL and distributed transactions in Aurora DSQL
supports: A transaction can contain only one DDL statement and cannot mix DDL and DML
A schema change updates the catalog version; a session holding an older cached catalog can receive SQLSTATE 40001 with OCC code OC001, and a retry typically succeeds

sources.title: Concurrency control in Aurora DSQL
supports: Optimistic concurrency control: conflicts are evaluated at commit time, without locks
A conflict is returned as SQLSTATE 40001; OC000 is a data conflict, OC001 a schema conflict
Of two transactions that modified the same row, the one that commits first succeeds
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is adjudicated at commit as if the transaction wrote the rows
AWS recommends retrying, with idempotent transactions, and random primary keys to avoid contention on a few keys

sources.title: Cluster quotas and database limits in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: 3,000 rows mutated per transaction, 10 MiB of data modified per write transaction, 5 minutes maximum transaction time, 60 minutes maximum connection duration
10,000 connections per cluster by default, 100 new connections per second with a burst of 1,000
1 database per cluster, 10 schemas per database, 1,000 tables per database, 24 indexes per table, 2 MiB per row
20 single-Region clusters per account per Region by default

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE TABLE
supports: CREATE TABLE supports IF NOT EXISTS, CHECK, DEFAULT, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES / FOREIGN KEY with referential actions, and identity columns
CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT actions count toward the per-transaction row limit

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: ALTER TABLE
supports: ADD COLUMN takes a column name and a data type; the supported syntax lists no constraint or default on that form
CHECK and FOREIGN KEY constraints added to an existing table must be NOT VALID and are validated with ALTER TABLE ASYNC ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
The listed actions include DROP NOT NULL but no SET NOT NULL and no change of a column's type

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE INDEX
supports: Index creation is always asynchronous, so the ASYNC keyword must be specified
CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC supports IF NOT EXISTS, INCLUDE, and a WHERE predicate

sources.title: Asynchronous indexes in Aurora DSQL
supports: CREATE INDEX ASYNC returns a job_id immediately
sys.jobs has job_id, status (submitted, processing, failed, completed), and details
A failed build leaves the index INVALID until it is dropped; completed and failed jobs are removed from sys.jobs after 30 minutes
sources.note: The page names sys.wait_for_job but shows no complete call, so the sample polls sys.jobs instead.

sources.title: Working with foreign key constraints in Aurora DSQL
supports: Foreign keys are checked against the transaction snapshot and again at commit; a violation by a concurrent transaction surfaces as a serialization error
Updating a non-key column of the referenced row does not conflict with an insert that references it
DML on referenced or referencing tables incurs extra reads

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Working with sequences and identity columns
supports: UUIDs are the recommended default identifier type; sequences and identity columns exist for when integers are needed
CREATE SEQUENCE requires an explicit CACHE of 1 or at least 65536 (stated on the CREATE SEQUENCE page, which was read too)

sources.title: Primary keys in Aurora DSQL
supports: A primary key cannot be changed or added after the table is created
For tables with many writes, AWS advises against monotonically increasing integer keys and for randomly distributed ones

sources.title: Authentication and authorization for Aurora DSQL
supports: dsql:DbConnectAdmin connects as the admin role; dsql:DbConnect connects as a custom database role
AWS IAM GRANT associates a database role with an IAM identity
After revoking the IAM permission, existing connections can stay authorized until they end

sources.title: Generating an authentication token in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: The token is the password, used only when a connection is established; an open connection stays valid after the token expires
Tokens expire after 15 minutes by default, one week at most
Generating a token is a local signing operation that does not contact AWS
The cluster endpoint has the form <cluster id>.dsql.<region>.on.aws
The JavaScript signer is DsqlSigner in @aws-sdk/dsql-signer, with getDbConnectAuthToken and getDbConnectAdminAuthToken

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Using database roles and IAM authentication
supports: CREATE ROLE ... WITH LOGIN, then AWS IAM GRANT <role> TO '<IAM role ARN>', then GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA and GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA
sys.iam_pg_role_mappings lists the mappings, with arn and pg_role_name columns

sources.title: Aurora DSQL Connectors for Node.js
supports: AWS publishes authentication plugins for node-postgres and for Postgres.js

sources.title: Aurora DSQL Connector for node-postgres
supports: The connector wraps node-postgres's Client and Pool and generates a token for each connection
A user named admin gets an admin token, any other user a regular one
sources.note: The sample does not use the connector; it passes the same signer to node-postgres directly, as the AWS Lambda sample does.

sources.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL cluster connectivity tools
supports: AWS lists driver samples for node-postgres, node-postgres on AWS Lambda, and Postgres.js
AWS lists an adapter for Drizzle ORM and samples for Prisma, Sequelize, and TypeORM

sources.title: aws-samples/aurora-dsql-samples: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: A Lambda function defined without a VPC connects with node-postgres, passing a function that calls DsqlSigner as the pool's password
The pool is kept in a module-level variable and shared between invocations
The sample builds the endpoint as <identifier>.dsql.<region>.on.aws and says an admin database role is not good practice for production

sources.title: Aurora DSQL cluster lifecycle
supports: A cluster without connection activity becomes Idle and then Inactive, where running resources are scaled to zero and data is kept
Connecting wakes it; the first connection to an Idle or Inactive cluster is slower
A backup needs an Active cluster

sources.title: Backup and restore for Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: Backups go through AWS Backup: full cluster backups, on demand or on a schedule with retention
A restore always creates a new cluster
sources.note: The page does not describe point-in-time recovery for Aurora DSQL.

sources.title: How billing works in Aurora DSQL
supports: Activity is metered in DPUs (compute, read, and write components) and storage in GB-month
Worked examples: a point lookup of 0.00675 DPU and a single-row insert of 0.06175 DPU
sources.note: The examples' DPU figures are used as stand-ins in the chapter's cost scenario. Nothing was measured.

sources.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL pricing
supports: Billed for DPUs and for storage in GB-month; an idle cluster incurs no DPU charges
Each month the first 100,000 DPUs and 1 GB of storage are free
Backups are billed through AWS Backup
sources.note: The page shows prices through a script; the numbers in the book come from the Price List. The page does not say whether the free tier ends.

sources.title: Managing and connecting to Amazon Aurora DSQL clusters using AWS PrivateLink
supports: The default cluster host name is a public DNS name; interface VPC endpoints are an option for private connectivity
Connecting through an endpoint's own DNS name or IP address does not support verify-full

sources.title: Troubleshooting issues in Aurora DSQL
supports: After an error during COMMIT the transaction might have committed; AWS says to design transactions to be idempotent
'Wrong user to action mapping' means the token type does not match the database role
A connection is rejected when the assumed role's credentials have expired, even if the token has not

sources.title: Considerations for working with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: GRANT and REVOKE changes reach existing connections within the connection lifetime; a new connection sees them at once
A connection should be refreshed to see schemas and tables created in another connection

sources.title: Release notes for Aurora DSQL
supports: Foreign key constraints were added on August 26, 2026
Identity columns and sequences were added on February 13, 2026; partial indexes on September 15, 2026

sources.title: Configuring SSL/TLS certificates for Aurora DSQL connections
supports: The server certificate chains to Amazon Root CA 1; AWS recommends verify-full for production

sources.title: AWS::DSQL::Cluster
supports: Properties: DeletionProtectionEnabled, KmsEncryptionKey, MultiRegionProperties, PolicyDocument, Tags; none is required
Ref returns the cluster identifier

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: src/provisioning/register-providers.ts
supports: No dedicated provider is registered for AWS::DSQL::Cluster, so it is handled through Cloud Control API
Dedicated providers are registered for the other types the chapter 13 stack uses
sources.note: src/provisioning/cc-protection-properties.ts at the same tag lists AWS::DSQL::Cluster with DeletionProtectionEnabled among Cloud-Control-routed types.

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-dsql module (type definitions)
supports: aws-cdk-lib/aws-dsql exports the generated CfnCluster (L1) and no higher-level construct
CfnCluster has deletionProtectionEnabled and exposes attrIdentifier, attrEndpoint, and attrResourceArn

sources.title: AWS Price List: Aurora DSQL, ap-northeast-1
supports: USD 0.00001 per DPU and USD 0.40 per GB-month of storage in Tokyo
Global SKUs priced at zero for the first 100,000 DPUs and the first GB-month

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon RDS and Aurora, ap-northeast-1
supports: db.t4g.micro PostgreSQL Single-AZ: USD 0.025 per hour; gp3 storage for PostgreSQL Single-AZ: USD 0.138 per GB-month
Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: USD 0.15 per ACU-hour; Aurora PostgreSQL storage: USD 0.12 per GB-month

sources.title: Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless
supports: Auto-pause is a minimum capacity of 0 ACUs; before it existed the lowest minimum was 0.5 ACUs
An instance pauses after 300 to 86,400 seconds without user connections (default 300)
A paused instance has no instance charge; storage is still charged
Resuming takes about 15 seconds, and 30 seconds or longer after more than 24 hours paused
An open user connection, an associated RDS Proxy, logical replication, or a zero-ETL integration keeps instances from pausing
Aurora PostgreSQL needs 16.3, 15.7, 14.12, 13.15 or higher

sources.title: How Aurora serverless works
supports: Capacity ranges from 0 to 256 ACUs; one ACU is about 2 GiB of memory with matching CPU and networking

sources.title: Using the Amazon RDS Data API
supports: Data API is an HTTP endpoint for an Aurora cluster that lets a Lambda function run SQL without being configured for a VPC
It uses database credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager
sources.note: Region and engine-version availability was not checked.

sources.title: Overview of backing up and restoring an Aurora DB cluster
supports: Aurora automated backups are continuous, with a retention period of 1 to 35 days, and cannot be disabled

sources.title: Working with a DB instance in a VPC
supports: An RDS DB instance is in a VPC and needs a DB subnet group

sources.title: Amazon RDS DB instance storage
supports: General Purpose gp3 storage for PostgreSQL starts at 20 GiB

sources.title: IAM database authentication for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL
supports: RDS offers IAM database authentication with 15-minute tokens as an option next to standard passwords

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
supports: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections for applications that open many of them

sources.title: Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS
supports: Point-in-time restore creates a new DB instance within the backup retention period

sources.title: PostgreSQL 16: Transaction Isolation
supports: Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL
Repeatable Read is implemented as snapshot isolation and raises 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'; the application should retry the whole transaction

sources.title: pg 8.23.1 and @types/pg 8.23.1
supports: Pool accepts a function returning a promise as password, and maxLifetimeSeconds (read in the pinned type definitions)
pg 8.23.1 was the latest version on the npm registry

sources.title: @aws-sdk/dsql-signer 3.1149.0
supports: DsqlSigner takes hostname, region, and optional credentials and expiresIn (read in the pinned type definitions)

sources.title: @electric-sql/pglite 0.5.8
supports: 0.5.8 was the latest version on the npm registry and declares no dependencies
Run locally, it reports PostgreSQL 18.3 and lets a second process open the same data directory (observed, not documented)
sources.note: Only the registry metadata was read and the package was run; its documentation was not.

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Migrations
supports: Migrations are numbered .sql files in a migrations folder, applied in order by Wrangler
Applied migrations are recorded in the d1_migrations table

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Global read replication
supports: Read replicas are asynchronously replicated and can be arbitrarily out of date; all writes go to the primary
Read replication is used only through the Sessions API, which provides sequential consistency within a session by passing bookmarks
withSession('first-primary') routes the first query to the primary

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Time Travel
supports: Time Travel restores a database to any minute within the last 30 days without scheduled backups

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: D1 Database (Workers Binding API)
supports: batch() runs its statements as one SQL transaction and rolls the whole sequence back if one fails

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: SQL statements
supports: D1 uses SQLite's query engine and is compatible with most of SQLite's SQL

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Pricing
supports: D1 bills rows read, rows written, and storage, with no charge for hours or capacity when no queries run

sources.title: Cloudflare Wrangler: d1 commands
supports: `wrangler d1 migrations apply` takes --local or --remote
If applying a migration results in an error, that migration is rolled back

definition.ja: schema の変更を順番つきのファイルにして、どこまで適用したかを DB 自身に記録するやり方。
definition.en: A schema change kept as a numbered file, with the database itself recording which ones have been applied.

definition.ja: 複数の SQL を「全部反映する」か「何も反映しない」のどちらかにまとめる単位。
definition.en: A group of SQL statements that takes effect entirely or not at all.

definition.ja: transaction が、開始した時点のデータを最後まで読み続ける分離の方式。PostgreSQL の REPEATABLE READ がこれにあたる。
definition.en: Isolation in which a transaction keeps reading the data as it was when the transaction started. PostgreSQL's REPEATABLE READ is this.

definition.ja: ロックで待たせず、commit のときに競合を調べて、負けた transaction を失敗させる方式。
definition.en: Checking for conflicts at commit instead of making transactions wait for locks; the transaction that loses fails.

definition.ja: ほかの transaction と競合したので commit できなかった、という DB からの応答。SQLSTATE は 40001。何も反映されていないので、transaction を最初からやり直す。
definition.en: The database's answer that a transaction could not commit because it conflicted with another. SQLSTATE 40001. Nothing was applied, so the transaction is run again from the start.

definition.ja: 2 つの transaction が同じデータを読んで判断し、別々の行に書いた結果、どちらか一方だけなら守れた条件が破れること。
definition.en: Two transactions decide from the same data and write different rows, breaking a condition that either alone would have kept.

definition.ja: DB の中の利用者。どの table に何ができるかは、この role への GRANT で決まる。IAM の role とは別のもの。
definition.en: A user inside the database. GRANTs to it decide what it may do to which table. Not the same thing as an IAM role.

definition.ja: 接続するときだけパスワードの代わりに渡す、IAM の認証情報で署名した期限つきの文字列。
definition.en: A time-limited string signed with IAM credentials, passed in place of a password when a connection is opened.

definition.ja: Distributed Processing Unit。Aurora DSQL が、SQL の実行にかかった計算、読み取り、書き込みをまとめて測る課金の単位。
definition.en: Distributed Processing Unit: the billing unit in which Aurora DSQL measures the compute, reads, and writes spent running SQL.

definition.ja: Aurora Capacity Unit。Aurora Serverless v2 の容量の単位で、1 ACU はおよそ 2 GiB のメモリと、それに見合う CPU とネットワーク。
definition.en: Aurora Capacity Unit: the capacity unit of Aurora Serverless v2. One ACU is about 2 GiB of memory with matching CPU and networking.

title.ja: Aurora DSQL: 月 100 万リクエストのノート API（DB の分だけ）
title.en: Aurora DSQL: a notes API at 1 million requests a month (database only)

ja: 読み取り 90 万件、書き込み 10 万件
読み取り 1 件は 0.00675 DPU と仮定（公式ドキュメントの point lookup の計算例の値）
書き込み 1 件は 0.18525 DPU と仮定（公式ドキュメントの 1 行 insert の計算例 0.06175 DPU の 3 倍。この章の作成は 3 行に書く）
この章の query で実測した値ではない
データは 1 GB
Lambda、API Gateway、ログ、backup は含めない
en: 900,000 reads and 100,000 writes
A read is assumed to cost 0.00675 DPU (the figure in the documentation's point-lookup example)
A write is assumed to cost 0.18525 DPU (three times the 0.06175 DPU of the documentation's single-row insert example; a create in this chapter writes three rows)
Not measured on this chapter's queries
1 GB of data
Lambda, API Gateway, logs, and backups are not included

summary.ja: 13章のコードを実際の Aurora DSQL に一度もつないでいない。未確認: 4 つの migration の SQL が受け付けられること（CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS、外部キー、CHECK、CREATE INDEX ASYNC IF NOT EXISTS）、CREATE INDEX ASYNC の応答から job_id を読めて sys.jobs を polling できること、AWS IAM GRANT と schema への GRANT で notes_api が読み書きできること、node-postgres の password に渡した関数で token が通ること、競合が node-postgres のエラーの code に 40001 として現れること、凍結から戻った実行環境で切れた接続がどう見えるか。手元の代用は PGlite（PostgreSQL 18.3）で、DSQL（PostgreSQL 16 互換）とは版も違う。
summary.en: The chapter 13 code has never been connected to a real Aurora DSQL cluster. Unconfirmed: that the four migrations are accepted (CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS, the foreign key, the CHECKs, CREATE INDEX ASYNC IF NOT EXISTS), that job_id can be read from the response to CREATE INDEX ASYNC and sys.jobs polled, that AWS IAM GRANT plus the schema GRANTs let notes_api read and write, that the token passes through the function given to node-postgres as password, that a conflict shows up as code 40001 on node-postgres's error, and how a dropped connection looks in an execution environment that was frozen. The local stand-in is PGlite (PostgreSQL 18.3), a different version from DSQL (PostgreSQL 16 compatible).

resume.ja: 学習用アカウントで vp run sql:infra:deploy、sql:db:migrate、sql:db:grant、sql:smoke を順に実行する。同じ note を同時に更新する負荷をかけ、sql:logs で "transaction retry" の行と 40001 を確認する。15 分以上あけて呼び、接続の張り直しを見る。結果を data/validation.json に記録し、vp run sql:infra:destroy で消す。
resume.en: In a practice account run vp run sql:infra:deploy, sql:db:migrate, sql:db:grant, and sql:smoke in that order. Put concurrent updates on one note and look for "transaction retry" lines and 40001 with sql:logs. Call again after more than 15 minutes and watch the reconnect. Record the results in data/validation.json and remove everything with vp run sql:infra:destroy.

summary.ja: cdkd 0.296.28 は AWS::DSQL::Cluster に専用の実装を持たず、Cloud Control API 経由で扱う。作成、Ref が cluster の identifier を返すこと、drift の読み戻し、削除が実際に動くかは未確認。13章の stack は Ref から endpoint と ARN を組み立てている。
summary.en: cdkd 0.296.28 has no dedicated provider for AWS::DSQL::Cluster and handles it through Cloud Control API. Whether create, Ref returning the cluster identifier, drift read-back, and delete work in practice is unconfirmed. The chapter 13 stack builds the endpoint and the ARN from Ref.

resume.ja: vp run sql:infra:deploy の後、output の ClusterEndpoint が <26 文字の id>.dsql.ap-northeast-1.on.aws の形であること、関数の環境変数と IAM policy の Resource が同じ cluster を指すことを確認する。vp run sql:infra:drift と sql:infra:destroy の結果も記録する。
resume.en: After vp run sql:infra:deploy, check that the ClusterEndpoint output has the form <26-character id>.dsql.ap-northeast-1.on.aws and that the function's environment variable and the IAM policy's Resource point at the same cluster. Record the results of vp run sql:infra:drift and sql:infra:destroy as well.

summary.ja: 13章の料金のシナリオは、1 リクエストあたりの DPU を公式ドキュメントの計算例から借りた仮定で、この章の query を測った値ではない。
summary.en: The chapter 13 cost scenario borrows its DPUs per request from the documentation's worked examples. They were not measured on this chapter's queries.

resume.ja: デプロイした cluster で EXPLAIN ANALYZE VERBOSE を使うか、CloudWatch の ComputeDPU、ReadDPU、WriteDPU を見て、作成、更新、一覧の 1 件あたりの DPU を測る。data/fragments/13.json の scenarios を直して apply し直す。
resume.en: On a deployed cluster use EXPLAIN ANALYZE VERBOSE, or the ComputeDPU, ReadDPU, and WriteDPU metrics in CloudWatch, to measure the DPUs of one create, one update, and one list. Correct the scenarios in data/fragments/13.json and apply it again.
